issues.description: signing_mode_enum helper logic differs from original RPC handler — safe_mode now selects CHIP_0002 even when is_hex=True
issues.detail: The new signing_mode_enum() returns CHIP_0002 when is_hex=True and safe_mode=True is not also handled first. Reading the order: is_hex+safe_mode -> CHIP_0002_HEX_INPUT (correct). But the default fallback case is CHIP_0002 which only matches not-is_hex AND safe_mode. Verify all four boolean combos map identically to the previous RPC behavior — particularly that the default fallback isn't reachable when is_hex=True+safe_mode=True.

issues.description: verify_signature raises ValueError on unknown mode instead of returning structured error like original code
issues.detail: Original RPC handler had the same raise-on-unknown-mode behavior, but the f-string error message references request.signing_mode in original code vs signing_mode in new code. The new util loses the raw string input (it received the validated enum) so error messages on misuse are less informative for callers passing an unmapped enum. Minor regression in diagnostics.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is an instance method but uses no instance state
issues.detail: Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic takes self but only calls a module-level function with module-level constants. This should be a @staticmethod or just remain a free function in signing.py. Making it an instance method couples the synthetic-key conversion to a Wallet instance unnecessarily and makes it harder to reuse from non-wallet code (the stated goal of this refactor).

issues.description: Stale/misleading docstring in verify_signature mentions ':param request:' but takes individual args
issues.detail: The function signature was changed to keyword-only individual arguments, but the docstring still says ':param request:' and ':return:'. This is copy-paste residue from the original RPC method. Update docstring to reflect new parameters or remove the stub.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address does not assert verify_signature result
issues.detail: The new test calls verify_signature but does not assert the response is valid. If verify_signature returns VerifySignatureResponse(isValid=False, error=...), the test silently passes. Add `assert response.isValid` to actually validate the round-trip.

issues.description: Duplicated synthetic-key derivation pattern across sign_message_by_address and sign_message_by_id
issues.detail: Both RPC handlers now repeat the same 3-line pattern: get_private_key -> convert_secret_key_to_synthetic -> sign_message. Given the goal is extraction/reuse, consider a single helper in signing.py that takes wallet_state_manager + puzzle_hash and returns a SignMessageResponse. Reduces drift risk between the two call sites.

review.summary: This PR is a clean extraction refactor of signing logic from the wallet RPC into chia/wallet/util/signing.py, with new test coverage for sign_message_by_id (NFT path) and sign_message_by_address. The behavioral refactor preserves the original mode-mapping logic but introduces a free function signing_mode_enum() that should be verified against all four (is_hex, safe_mode) combinations. Minor concerns: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is an instance method without using instance state, the new test_sign_message_by_address never asserts isValid, and stale docstrings reference ':param request:' after the signature change. No P0 correctness issues found; the refactor looks functionally equivalent to the original code.
